rationale: Short turn reconciling the sweep investigation with the new finding. The sweep's own event set is what produced the three apply-side rejections behind the asserted availability defect (CheckRun 880f6a9dbf1e44209e75c837b81e27ad indices 17-19), yet the four invariants the sweep checks reported no violation there, because none of them covers whether a committed configuration change is applicable at the node that must apply it. That is a real gap in what the sweep measures rather than a contradiction in its results, so I register it under the sweep investigation instead of restating the earlier answer, and note what a check would have to observe: the entry types and terms a node applies, its tracker state at apply time, and whether the change is admissible for that state. No experiment is requested: that check belongs with the deterministic prefix registered on @joint_apply_order, not with another randomized run.

gaps.question: The four invariants this sweep checks (at most one leader per term, no committed (index,term) contradiction, committed-index monotonicity, applied<=committed) all held in the revision whose event set also produced three apply-side rejections of a committed configuration change (CheckRun 880f6a9dbf1e44209e75c837b81e27ad indices 17-19). Since those invariants are silent about whether a committed configuration change is admissible at the node that must apply it, which observable property would have to be checked to make this sweep's safety account cover the availability shape it produced, and can that property be stated without re-implementing the target's admission logic (for example by checking that each applied EntryConfChangeV2 is accepted, that the node's tracker state before and after is consistent with the entry, and that no node applies an entry its own state rejects)?
